section: Perspectives in Education · Ch — Types of Curriculum
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: One of NCF 2005's core recommendations was to 'connect knowledge to life' rather than teach subjects in isolation. This principle chiefly means:

options.option_text: Relating classroom learning to students' real-life experiences and surroundings, making learning meaningful rather than abstract
Ensuring students memorise the maximum possible number of textbook facts
Focusing purely on preparing students for competitive exams
Removing all practical or activity-based components from the syllabus

explanation: NCF 2005's 'connect knowledge to life' principle emphasises meaningful, contextual learning tied to real experiences, rather than abstract, rote, exam-only content.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch — Types of Curriculum
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: NCF 2005 recommended that examinations should shift away from testing only:

options.option_text: Rote memorisation, towards testing understanding and the ability to apply and analyse concepts
Understanding, towards testing only pure memorisation

explanation: NCF 2005 pushed for exams that assess genuine understanding, application, and higher-order thinking rather than rote reproduction of textbook content.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch — Types of Curriculum
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: NCF 2005's guiding principle of 'enriching the curriculum' specifically refers to:

options.option_text: Going beyond textbooks to include local knowledge, real-life skills, and diverse resources
Adding more chapters purely to increase textbook page count
Restricting the syllabus strictly to textbook content only
Removing art and physical education from schools

explanation: Curriculum enrichment means going beyond a single prescribed textbook to draw on local knowledge, community resources, and varied learning materials, making education richer and more relevant.
